set.headline: Turning monthly savings into more happier and healthier years together
set.brief: Help a premium, best-in-class insurer stand apart in a category where every brand competes on coverage statistics.
set.reframe: The product isn't protection against what might go wrong. It's an investment in more time with someone you treat as family.
set.contribution: I led the repositioning from a necessary-evil purchase to an investment in pet longevity, and built the Love Longer platform and messaging system.

figures.label: Raised at Fetch's inaugural NYC gala, which the campaign contributed to

diagram.title: Where the category stood, and where it didn't
diagram.caption: A competitive audit mapped every major player. They clustered in one quadrant. The open space was the only place a premium brand could credibly stand.

set.headline: Giving New Yorkers permission to not mind their own business
set.brief: Use the World Cup's scale to raise awareness of human trafficking and help people recognize and respond to the signs.
set.reframe: The barrier comes before awareness. In New York and New Jersey, minding your own business is a social norm, so the work had to interrupt the instinct to look away.
set.contribution: I developed the creative strategy, Don't Mind Your Own Business, for HMH's FIFA World Cup sponsorship.

figures.label: Visitors expected in the region during the tournament

diagram.title: Going upstream of awareness
diagram.caption: Instead of one more voice telling people to stay alert, the strategy targeted the behavior that comes before seeing anything at all.

shifts.to: Interrupt the instinct not to look

set.headline: Transforming back-office payments into a CFO's growth lever
set.brief: Sell two B2B payment products in a category where everyone promises faster cash flow and lower costs.
set.reframe: CFOs use working capital to fund growth. The products already delivered that, so the messaging had to move from what they do to what they make possible.
set.contribution: I led brand and sales enablement for American Express Global Commercial Services, and built monthly competitive intelligence across nine major financial brands.

figures.label: Messaging playbooks, for Buyer Initiated Payments and One AP
Financial brands tracked in monthly competitive intelligence

diagram.title: Three shifts for Buyer Initiated Payments
diagram.caption: Each shift is mapped to where the buyer is, from the first need for a better way to pay suppliers to the final business case.

set.headline: Showing how Gen-Z insight helps inform product marketing decisions
set.brief: Build foundational insight into 21- to 29-year-old drinkers and turn it into a plan for winning with them.
set.reframe: A 21-year-old moving out and a 29-year-old new parent share a birth window, not a mindset. Strategy built on the generational label would miss them.
set.role: Associate Strategist, The Mix Global & AKQA
set.contribution: I led the digital ethnography analysis and the New York and Phoenix field workshops.

figures.label: Young drinkers in a seven-day digital ethnography

diagram.title: A five-phase research architecture
diagram.caption: Built to move from observation to action. Every insight had to earn its way into the playbook.
steps: Immersive workshops in New York and Phoenix

set.headline: Turning one Apollo story into ten conversations that start with the client
set.brief: Make Apollo's communication land with pensions, sovereign wealth funds, wirehouses, RIAs and more, when every material led with credentials.
set.reframe: Each audience is making a different decision. Keep one positioning, and adapt the emphasis to each audience's pressure and the assumption worth challenging.
set.contribution: I built the audience segmentation messaging playbook, giving brand and product marketing teams a shared system for who they're talking to and why.
